meta.title: MERIT Clean Architecture: rings and dependency direction

views.label: Web request ring crossing
views.note: Web binds a request, checks the permission policy, calls one Application service, which applies Domain rules.

views.label: Ports and adapters
views.note: Application owns the I*Data ports; Merit.Data.SqlServer implements them with Dapper calls to stored procedures.

views.label: Background entry point
views.note: The Worker is a second entry point: it claims queued jobs and runs Application job code under the requesting user's scope.

views.label: Domain core
views.note: Merit.Domain references nothing: population, normalization, thresholds, classification, matching and residence rules.

boundaries.label: Outer ring: entry points, adapters, contracts

cards.title: Presentation / entry points
items: Merit.Web: thin MVC controllers (Razor + htmx), JSON API under /api/v1, the Angular host under /app/, security headers and CSP
Merit.Worker: BackgroundService that claims queued jobs and a cluster-detection scheduler
Both are composition roots: AddMeritApplication() plus AddMeritSqlServer(), so they reference the Data project for wiring only

cards.title: Application / use cases
items: Services (Person, Result, Case, Intake, Report, Profile ...) validate input and check permissions
Ports: IAccountData, IPersonData, IResultData, ICaseData, IWorkData, IIntakeData ... implemented outside
Jobs: JobDispatcher runs intakeBatch, extractRun and clusterDetection

cards.title: Domain core
items: Pure C#: population, result normalization, thresholds, case classification, matching, residence planning, extract formats
No project or package references, so every ring can depend on it and it depends on none

cards.title: Infrastructure / persistence
items: Merit.Data.SqlServer references Application and implements its ports with Dapper
Every call is a stored procedure; each connection sets a read-only SESSION_CONTEXT that row-level security filters by

cards.title: Shared contracts and the inward rule
items: Merit.Contracts holds the API DTO records and references nothing; only Web uses them, so Application never sees transport types
Every arrow points inward or into a port: Web and Worker to Application, Application to Domain, Data to the ports Application owns (dependency inversion)
DI wiring is not drawn: Web and Worker register the adapters at startup, and no controller or job calls Data directly (architecture tests enforce this)
